What counts as a unique customer?
One phone number, once a month. If the same person calls back five times in March, that is one customer. Two different people is two. Spam and wrong numbers don't count at all.
Are there charges for minutes, calls, or tokens?
No. We never meter minutes. A thirty-second wrong number and a nine-minute booking cost exactly the same, nothing extra. That's the whole point of billing per customer.
What happens if I go over?

Nothing breaks. Extra customers bill at your plan's own rate: 79¢ on Starter, 26¢ on Growth, 15¢ on Scale. There's no penalty rate, and we tell you when a bigger plan would be cheaper than staying where you are.
How does this compare to an answering service?

A live answering service runs about $1.50 to $1.90 a minute. Even at four-minute calls, Starter works out to about 13¢ a minute, around a twelfth of the cost, and it answers every hour of every day. The longer your calls run, the cheaper we get, the opposite of metered billing.
Do I have to pay for a phone number?
No. Every plan includes a local number, and you can keep your existing one instead by forwarding it to us.
What counts as an external tool?
Anything you connect or build: an API, an MCP server, or a code block you write yourself. Each one counts once no matter how many workers use it. Transfers, hang-ups and call handling never count.
One specialist inside your agent: a booker, a message taker, a knowledge expert. Your operator and greeter never count against the limit, so the number on the plan is the workers you add yourself.
Describe the change you want in plain English and Gabi rewrites your agent: new questions, new steps, a different greeting. No forms, no rebuild, unlimited on every plan.

Test calls we run against your agent so you can check it behaves before it answers a real customer. Starter gets a base allowance, Growth 5× that, Scale 20×. Talking to Gabi is never metered, only the test runs count, and you can top up $5 at a time.
Better: a free demo agent. Build it, test it, hear it answer, and only pay when you connect a number. Nothing is locked while you're trying it out.
